text:
maria: Heads-up — we're scheduling a midnight burst canary to validate the new batching kernels. Plan is staggered rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% over ~30m. Need router, runtime, and console pin coordination. Any objections? :eyes:

sahil: +1, fine with staggering. What's the rollback window look like? We should avoid >2m p99 regression spikes.

jon: Agree on staging. Two asks: 1) runtime needs a short-lived pin for the kernel variant, 2) router needs a traffic shard tag so we can route only canary traffic.

maria: Correct. Runtime pin = model-serving:kernel-v2-temp, TTL 1h. Router tag = canary-nightburst-2026-03-22. Console: we want a dedicated per-model dashboard slice so we don't mix metrics.

deploybot: deploybot: scheduling wave at 2026-03-22T00:30Z. Canary waves: t+0 10% (10m), t+10m 30% (10m), t+20m 60% (10m). Auto-rollback on error rate >2% or latency >2x baseline for 3 consecutive 60s buckets.

elaine: Ops note: if we see sustained qps backpressure due to batching changes, we should have an immediate throttle. Can ops-bot hold a manual choke?

ops-bot: ops-bot: I can insert a token bucket throttle on the router shard. Command: `/ops throttle set canary-nightburst-2026-03-22 rate=250rps burst=500` — will stand by until someone runs `/ops throttle clear`.

kate: Console folks: I'll create the dashboard slice and a short alert rule for prompt-quality regressions (KL divergence on embeddings >0.15). Link to slice will be posted before t-15m.

maria: Two more things — release notes: call out kernel change + batch-size heuristics, and explicitly mark as "non-persistent pin" so Dedicated doesn't assume long-term commit. Also add manual rollback steps in notes.

jon: For router: we'll add a header flip as a safety fallback. If deploybot signals rollback, router will remove canary-nightburst header rule and traffic drops to 0%. Who owns that change?

sahil: I'll own header flip (router config PR ready). Will post the exact curl for ops to run in case we need immediate drop. Example: `curl -X POST https://router.ops/api/route/remove -d '{"tag":"canary-nightburst-2026-03-22"}'`

maria: Good. Quick preflight checklist (t-30m): runtime pin applied, router tag live but 0% traffic, dashboard slice created, deploybot scheduled, ops-bot throttle ready. Can everyone ack?

elaine: ack — ops-bot throttle ready, monitoring on-call standing by.

kate: ack — dashboard slice will be up at t-20m.

jon: ack — router PR merged to canary branch and staged.

sahil: ack — rollback curl posted in the PR comments.

deploybot: deploybot: wave created and locked. Will not start automated wave until an explicit :start: reaction on this thread by an approver.

maria: tagging @here for approvals. If no objections by t-10m, we'll proceed with the manual :start: and follow deploybot wave. :thumbsup:

jon: added :thumbsup: — ready to start at your signal.

maria: final note — keep the kernel pin TTL tight. If post-burst looks stable, we'll follow the normal model-onboarding path for a permanent variant. Otherwise, roll back and open an eval ticket.

sahil: copying release notes snippet into the PR.

maria: thanks everyone. I'll post the start reaction at t when ready.

deploybot: deploybot: reminder scheduled at t-15m to this thread.
